_meta.what_this_is: One image strip decomposed into three channels: Y (luma, brightness) and Cb, Cr (chroma, color). Each channel is deliberately given the IDENTICAL high-frequency pattern [16, 235, 16, 235, ...], so that subsampling any one of them (average adjacent pairs, then reconstruct) produces exactly the same raw reconstruction error. That isolates the one thing that actually differs between the channels: the perceptual weight -- how much the eye's acuity depends on detail in that channel. Luma dominates; each chroma channel contributes little.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. The identical patterns and the perceptual weights are hand-authored so the raw errors are exactly equal and the perceptual costs are exact and checkable; every error is computed in chroma.py. The weights (Y 0.85, Cb/Cr 0.075) reflect that the eye is far more sensitive to brightness detail than color detail -- the basis of chroma subsampling.
_meta.format: channels: {name: samples}; weights: {name: perceptual sensitivity}; roles/order for display; luma and chroma_example name the two channels the cost view compares.
